Auto-answered by the orchestrator clarify-respond workflow.

DECISIONS:
Q1: A
Q2: A
Q3: B
Q4: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: Items 1-3 are the core request in tele-funtoken-msg-scoring#4606. Item 4 is described as an alternative or complement. It touches a different pipeline (`validation-refresh.yml`, which runs with credentials blanked), and the nightly refresh is already being fixed separately. Keeping it out of this issue keeps the change small. Note it as a follow-up in the PR body.
Q2: GitHub cannot read repo variables inside `on.schedule`, so every consumer that opts in gets the same fixed cron. Weekly limits spending across consumers, and one consumer has gone about four weeks without a run, so weekly is a large improvement. Option C adds a second variable without much benefit.
Q3: The issue's main worry is cost when the sync reaches every consumer. A scheduled run on the default branch has no project to repair, so diagnose and self-heal would spend money and might commit fixes without anyone asking. Grep found no existing switch in `scripts/validate_process.sh` to skip generate or diagnose. Only `MAX_SELF_HEAL_ATTEMPTS` exists (line 322). The scheduled path therefore needs a new deterministic-mode gate.
Q4: Option B does not reach consumers. `SCHEDULED_CHECK_WORKFLOW_NAMES` (`scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:82`) and `SCHEDULED_CHECK_WORKFLOW_FILES` (line 189) only cover this repo's own `workflow_run` reports from `nightly-validation-selftest.yml`, so a consumer's red run would still be silent. Option A puts the failure where the consumer will see it. Giving the issue a pipeline exclusion label stops Q3's no-LLM choice from being undone by clarify→plan→implement picking the issue up.

EXECUTION PLAN (required for any non-letter decision):
Q1:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - workflow-templates/ai-validate.yml (today it only has `workflow_dispatch`)
    - .github/workflows/validate.yml
  steps:
    - Implement only items 1-3. Do not change `validation-refresh.yml` or `scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py`.
    - In the PR body, say that item 4 (a sink for red `validation-refresh` results) is deferred to a follow-up.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: n/a
  equivalence_argument: n/a
  reversibility: Item 4 can be added later without touching this change.
Q2:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - workflow-templates/ai-validate.yml
  steps:
    - Add `schedule: - cron: "17 4 * * 1"` (Monday 04:17 UTC). The odd minute avoids the busy top of the hour.
    - Gate the job with `if: github.event_name != 'schedule' || vars.AI_VALIDATE_SCHEDULE_ENABLED == 'true'`. When the variable is unset or anything other than `true`, the job is skipped and no runner starts.
    - Scheduled runs have no inputs. The existing `inputs.x || default` fallbacks already pass `tracking_issue=0`, `target_ref=''`, `compose_file=docker-compose.yml` and `validation_timeout=15`, and the run-name renders `[tracking:0]`. Keep these fallbacks.
    - Add a contract test for the cron, the gate expression and the job-level predicate. Wrapper/template parity tests must still pass.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: n/a
  equivalence_argument: n/a
  reversibility: Change the cron string in the template, or set the variable to `false`.
Q3:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/validate.yml (the `tracking_issue` validation at lines 764-771 accepts `0`; `MAX_SELF_HEAL_ATTEMPTS` is passed at line 1272)
    - scripts/validate_process.sh (`MAX_SELF_HEAL_ATTEMPTS` at lines 322-327; the self-heal gate at line 911)
  steps:
    - Detect scheduled mode in `validate.yml` from `github.event_name == 'schedule'`. A called workflow keeps the caller's event, so no new `workflow_call` input is needed, and the wrapper and the reusable workflow cannot get out of sync at release time.
    - In scheduled mode, set `MAX_SELF_HEAL_ATTEMPTS=0`, and add a new script-defaulted switch (for example `VALIDATE_DETERMINISTIC_ONLY`, default `false` in `validate_process.sh`). When it is on, the generate, discover and diagnose model phases are skipped, and only the committed `.ai/validate.yml` and the rendered harness run. Log the reason for each skipped phase.
    - When no harness or manifest exists, report a distinct status (for example `raw_status=harness_missing`) and do not call a model.
    - Check end to end that `tracking_issue=0` with an empty `target_ref` checks out the default branch and posts no tracking-issue comments or labels.
    - Add contract tests for scheduled-mode env propagation and for skipping the model phases.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: n/a
  equivalence_argument: The deterministic run still runs the consumer's compose build and tests on the default branch, which is the coverage #4606 asks for. Repair stays with `/revalidate` or project validation.
  reversibility: A later change can allow generate or diagnose in scheduled mode by flipping the new switch for that event.
Q4:
  strategy: derive_from_repo
  inputs:
    - .github/workflows/validate.yml (end-of-run summary steps around lines 1501-1595)
    - scripts/tg_helpers.sh (WARNING means a person has to act)
    - .github/workflows/clarify.yml / internal-clarify.yml (the existing `ai:retro` / `ai:security-audit` exclusion gate)
  steps:
    - Add a step that runs only in scheduled mode, after validation. When the run is red or `harness_missing`, it finds the pipeline-authored issue whose body starts with `<!-- ai:scheduled-validation:v1 -->`. Only issues authored by the `GH_PAT` login count. If none is open, it opens one with the label `ai:scheduled-validation-failed`.
    - While the issue stays open, edit its body in place on each red run with the run link, status, failing tests and default-branch SHA. Do not add a new comment per run.
    - Send one Telegram WARNING only when the issue is opened.
    - When a later scheduled run passes, add one comment and close the issue.
    - Add `ai:scheduled-validation-failed` to the label contract, and to the clarify exclusion lists next to `ai:retro` / `ai:security-audit`, so the issue never enters clarify→plan→implement.
    - Run all reads and writes through `gh_api_retry` / `gh_retry`, failing open (warn and keep the run's real conclusion). Use one paginated issue listing per run (§14).
    - Add contract tests for the marker, the dedup and close behaviour, and the exclusion.
  replaces_acceptance_criterion: n/a
  equivalence_argument: n/a
  reversibility: Removing the exclusion label lets an operator send a specific failure through the normal pipeline.

SETUP REQUIRED:
- AI_VALIDATE_SCHEDULE_ENABLED (variable): a consumer sets it to `true` to opt in to the weekly validation run. Until then the scheduled job is skipped and nothing runs or spends.

Assumptions and context notes:
- The consumer must also receive the updated wrapper through the `@stable` sync. Consumers with `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=false` will not get the `schedule:` trigger.
- tele-funtoken-msg-scoring#4606 is now closed as not planned. This issue carries its request forward.
- I did not check whether `validate_process.sh` creates fix issues when `tracking_issue=0`. The implementer should confirm that scheduled mode creates none, because Q4's single issue is the only place a failure should be reported.
